messages.subject: paths in ArrayExplorer
parts:
1. Though on OS X, ArrayExplorer seems to assume a Windows machine -
or what do the backslashes in the strangely concateneted path at the
end mean?

process(ae); display(ae)
[1] FALSE
2007-09-11 14:56:04.962 open[519] No such file: /Users/mbaudis/
Documents/AachenArrays/AA_working/\Users\mbaudis\Documents\AachenArrays
\AA_working\reports\raw\ArrayExplorer.html

Files are there, though.

2. ArrayExplorer assumes the "includes" to be in "../../
includes" (rel. to index.html), but they are in "../includes". Works
after moving the includes directory one up.

Michael.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] paths in ArrayExplorer
parts:
On 9/11/07, mbaudis <mba...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> 1. Though on OS X, ArrayExplorer seems to assume a Windows machine -
> or what do the backslashes in the strangely concateneted path at the
> end mean?

Developed on Windows & Linux, but OS X. However, it should detect
system specific separators. My best guess right now is that this has
to do with getAbsolutePath()/getRelativePath() in my R.utils package.

>
> process(ae); display(ae)
> [1] FALSE
> 2007-09-11 14:56:04.962 open[519] No such file: /Users/mbaudis/
> Documents/AachenArrays/AA_working/\Users\mbaudis\Documents\AachenArrays
> \AA_working\reports\raw\ArrayExplorer.html

Can you please cut'n'paste more of the ouput; I assume you do use
process(ae, verbose) above.

Also, it obviously fails with the pathname because there should also
be a data set name in /reports/<data set name>/raw/ArrayExplorer.html.
This also explains why ../../includes/ is indeed correct. Please let
me know what:

print(ae)

gives. This might all be related to one thing.

>
> Files are there, though.
>
> 2. ArrayExplorer assumes the "includes" to be in "../../
> includes" (rel. to index.html), but they are in "../includes". Works
> after moving the includes directory one up.

Hmm... that should be ArrayExplorer.html and not index.html.

What's your sessionInfo()? Also, be sure everything is right with
your code, please paste your complete script up until process(ae); it
shouldn't be many lines of code.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Michael.

>
